title: Leek & Potato Soup with Crispy Purple Potato–Leek Topping

items.text: 3 large leeks (whites for soup, dark green tops for topping)
1.5 lb Little Trios potatoes (1 pack — red, yellow, and purple)
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
½ cup extra creamy oat milk
½ cup neutral oil (vegetable or canola), for frying

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Sort the 1.5 lb potatoes: purple for the topping, red and yellow for the soup. Rinse all of them.
Cut the root ends off the 3 leeks. Cut off the dark green tops and set them aside. Slice the white and light green parts in half lengthwise, then into thin half-moons.

Slice a handful of dark green tops into very thin, matchstick-width strips. Put the strips and the half-moons in separate bowls of cold water and swish. Let sit 2 minutes so grit sinks, then scoop out by hand. Pat the strips completely dry — wet leeks splatter in hot oil.
Cut the purple potatoes into ½-inch cubes. Toss with the 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt. Spread in one layer on a baking sheet. Roast 20–25 minutes, flipping once halfway.
steps.donenessCue: Edges browned and crisp, a fork slides in easily.

steps.text: While those roast, halve the soup potatoes (quarter bigger ones). Leave the skins on. Peel and smash the 3 garlic cloves.
Melt the 3 tbsp butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the leek half-moons, garlic, and 1 tsp salt. Stir occasionally, about 10 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Soft, floppy, shiny — not browned. Brown edges? Turn the heat down.

steps.text: Add the soup potatoes, 3½ cups broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil over high heat, then lower to a gentle simmer and cover. Start checking at 15 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: A fork slides into the potatoes with no resistance.

steps.text: While the soup simmers, heat the ½ cup neutral oil in a small pan over medium. Add the dried leek strips and stir often, 2–4 minutes. Drain on a paper towel and salt right away.
steps.donenessCue: Golden at the edges, mostly stopped bubbling. Pull before they brown or they’ll taste bitter.

steps.text: Turn off the heat and remove the bay leaf. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth. Regular blender? Fill it only halfway, hold the lid down with a towel, and blend in batches.

With the heat off or on low, stir in the ½ cup oat milk and ½ tsp pepper. Don’t let it boil after this. Taste and add salt a pinch at a time until it tastes rich instead of flat. If the oat milk made it a little sweet, add a small squeeze of lemon.
Ladle into bowls. Right before serving, spoon the purple potatoes and crispy leeks into the center — last-minute keeps them crunchy and keeps the purple from bleeding into the soup.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: If most of your potatoes are purple: put the extra purples in the soup and embrace the color. Stir in 1–2 tsp lemon juice after the oat milk — acid pushes the pigment pinker instead of gray. Use mostly white leek parts in the soup; the green muddies the color.
Save leftover dark green leek tops in the freezer for making broth.
storage: Soup: cool completely, fridge up to 4 days. Reheat over medium-low, thinning with broth. To freeze (up to 3 months), freeze before adding the oat milk; stir it in after reheating. Crispy leeks: room temperature, airtight, paper-towel lined, 1–2 days — don’t refrigerate. Purple potatoes: fridge separately up to 4 days; re-crisp at 400°F (oven or air fryer) 5–8 minutes. Always store toppings apart from the soup. Too thick? Splash of broth or water. Too thin? Simmer uncovered a few minutes.
